rose.means: the ask — CTA only, never earlier

color.rule: One accent per beat. Two accents share a frame only in a before/after split.

safe_zones.note: Only the CTA arrow may cross into player chrome — it points at the real comment button.

layouts.statement: Full-bleed statement: type only on the ground, centred in the content band. Nothing else in frame.
layouts.card: Product card: rounded accent-filled card holding a small kicker and the name.
layouts.stat: Stat slab: one giant numeral above its unit word, on the bare ground.
layouts.negation: Negation list: short 'No X.' lines stacked, accumulating one per cut, unrevealed lines at 16% opacity.
layouts.split: Split diagram: two rounded panes side by side — old way in peach on the left, new way in lilac on the right.
layouts.flow: Flow row: pill-shaped nodes joined by arrows, revealed left to right.
layouts.keyboard: Analogy device: a mock phone keyboard suggestion strip, one key highlighted in the beat accent.
layouts.screen: Screen inset: dark rounded terminal card with an accent glow ring; lines appear one per cut and stay.
layouts.cta: Comment card: accent-filled card with the comment word, plus a hand-drawn arrow to the player's comment button.

beats.name: HOOK
beats.role: Break an accepted constraint with an impossible-sounding question. No logo, no name.
beats.narration: What if the thing everyone calls artificial intelligence isn't actually intelligent at all?

beats.name: REVEAL
beats.role: Name the thing once. Music enters here, not before.
beats.narration: It's autocomplete. Very, very good autocomplete.

beats.name: SPEC
beats.role: Credibility. Three numbers on separate frames, then the negation list.
beats.narration: A modern model has read fifteen trillion words and stores four hundred billion numbers. It does exactly one thing: guess what comes next. No memory. No goals.

beats.name: TURN
beats.role: The re-hook. Three words on a near-empty frame at the drop-off point.

beats.name: MECH
beats.role: Show the naive approach, then the real one. Longest beat; only beat allowed two accents.
beats.narration: Instead of looking anything up, it turns your words into numbers, pushes them through billions of tiny weights, and predicts the single most likely next word. Then it repeats.

beats.name: ANALOGY
beats.role: Restate the mechanism with something the viewer already uses. New visual language.
beats.narration: Think of it like your phone's keyboard. It doesn't know what you mean. It knows what usually comes next.

beats.name: HOWTO
beats.role: Exactly four steps, accumulating so the last frame shows all four.
beats.narration: Using it well is simple: Give it a role. Give it context. Give it an example. Ask for one thing.

beats.name: BONUS
beats.role: One extra capability aimed at the viewer about to leave. Earns saves.
beats.narration: Or paste in your own document first, and it answers from your material instead of guessing from training data.

beats.name: THESIS
beats.role: Zoom out: not X, but Y → direction of travel → who wins. Slowest cuts.
beats.narration: The real shift isn't that machines started thinking. It's that guessing the next word, at scale, looks a lot like thinking. And that's enough to be useful.

beats.name: CTA
beats.role: Comment-gate, not a link. Hold the last frame so it loops into frame one.
beats.narration: Comment DUMMY and I'll send you the full guide.
